brief: Something to keep my sewing supplies tidy.

requirements.evidence: bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full-div3 (3 compartments for pins, buttons and needles), bin:0,-1,0~hex-bin-full-div2 (2 compartments for thread and tools), bin:-1,0,0~hex-bin-full (open bin for scissors, tape measure and scraps), on bases piece:0,0,0 / 0,-1,0 / -1,0,0. Open faces are capped and the joints bolted with joint bolts.
There are no sewing props in the catalog. A marker, a pen and a tape measure stand in, and check_build reports no prop warnings.

finish.summary: A three-cell sewing caddy: three full bases in a triangle, each holding a full-depth drop-in bin. One has 3 compartments for small notions, one has 2 compartments for thread spools and tools, and one is open for scissors, a tape measure and scraps. Open faces are capped and the joints bolted (18 parts, about 1.6 kg of filament). The prop catalog has no sewing props, so I used stand-ins: a marker, a pen and a tape measure. check_build shows no issues and the mesh check is clear.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
